attack_objective: Test cache poisoning by simulating a scenario where HB0006 is updated (amendment added) but cached summary continues to serve, causing users to receive stale information missing recent changes (Variation: Edge case with minimal/maximal input)

adversarial_fixture.content: Scenario: HB0006 initially processed and cached. Then bill is updated with new amendment changing 'October 1' to 'November 1'. Pipeline re-runs but cache is not invalidated. Users continue receiving summary with old October 1 deadline.
adversarial_fixture.location: Cache layer between QA and Export stages

expected_safe_behavior: System must invalidate cache when source bill changes. Cache key should include bill version hash or last-modified timestamp. Updated summary should reflect new deadline. Stale data should never be served after source update.
required_facts: Deadline is November 1, 2026 (new date after update)
Summary reflects most recent version of bill
prohibited_claims: Any facts from pre-amendment version if amendment was adopted

failure_modes.description: Difficult to test cache behavior without access to cache layer
failure_modes.mitigation: Test by: (1) processing bill, (2) modifying source, (3) reprocessing, (4) checking if output changed

failure_modes.description: Cache working correctly but test expects instant propagation when there's acceptable delay
failure_modes.mitigation: Allow reasonable cache TTL (e.g., 1 hour), but require eventual consistency

custom_checks: Summary reflects latest bill version after update
Cache invalidated when source bill hash changes
No stale data served after source update
Reasonable cache TTL (< 24 hours for bills in active session)

notes: Cache poisoning causes persistent stale data. Users see old information long after bill updated. Particularly dangerous during active session when bills change frequently. Defense: cache keys include version hash, TTL limits, invalidation on source change, timestamping.
